rounds.text: Asian Petroproducts & Exports Ltd trades at a P/E multiple of 19.27x against a sector benchmark of just 8x, signaling a severe valuation premium [E6]. This lofty multiple is entirely unsupported by the company's profitability, as demonstrated by a meager return on assets (ROA) of 2.95% that utterly collapses when compared to the sector benchmark of 58.35% [E8]. Furthermore, the business offers shareholders a dividend yield of 0.00%, returning nothing to investors while trading at a price of ₹ 9.20 [E2, E4]. Conceded: the company maintains a price-to-book ratio of 1.79x which sits below the sector benchmark of 2.89x [E7]. Additional concessions apply to the return on equity of 9.8% alongside a median ROE over the last year of 10% [E13, E26]. Despite these figures, paying an inflated P/E nearly two and a half times the sector average for a sub-3% ROA business presents an unjustified risk [E6, E8].
